facts.text: 公開時の投稿に、もう一人の共同創業者も応答した。1万米ドルを住所変換に払えない開発者でも使えるようにすることが狙いで、データの使い方に制限を設けていないと説明した。
大量の住所を一度の接続でまとめて処理する方式を紹介した。利用者joelverhagenは通信往復の削減を歓迎した。
創業者は、無作為に選んだ100住所の試験で、90件がGoogle Maps APIの返す位置から1マイル以内だったと説明した。一方で利用者からは、精度、海外対応、無料の代替との差を問う発言があった。
Michele Hansenが最高経営責任者兼共同創業者、Mathias Hansenが最高技術責任者兼共同創業者。夫婦が率いる小さなチームで運営し、意図して小さな会社にしていると説明する。
2014年の開始以降、15万人以上が利用し、数十億件の住所を処理したと説明。
最初の接続仕様の版を現在も維持し、互換性を壊す変更は別の版へ分ける方針を説明。
公式サイトの法人表記はDotsquare LLC、所在地はVirginia州Norfolk。
住所と座標の相互変換、住所整形、地域・選挙区・時間帯などの付加情報を提供。対象は米国、カナダ、メキシコ、英国。
Sherwin-WilliamsのRan Dingは、12,000住所を他社で処理すると50〜60米ドル、Googleへの接続をExcelで自作すると遅く頻繁に停止したと公式推薦文で述べる。
SimplyRETSのChristopher Reichertは、数年にわたり中核設備として組み込み、問題調査の時間を大きく減らしたと公式推薦文で述べる。
従量プランは1日2,500単位まで無料、超過分は1,000単位あたり1米ドル。住所変換1件と追加情報の付加は別の課金単位。前月の利用分を翌月1日に請求する。
従量プランは米国・カナダ・メキシコ向け。利用者1人、接続キー3個、毎分1,000件、同時処理ファイル1件の上限がある。
Flex 350は月350,000単位で月325米ドルまたは年3,250米ドル。Flex 650は月600米ドルまたは年6,000米ドル、Flex 850は月775米ドルまたは年7,750米ドル。
別途購入した処理単位は失効しない。定額契約に含む単位の繰越は契約が有効な間に限る。
従量料金を1,000単位あたり0.50米ドルから1米ドルへ改定。1日2,500単位の無料枠は維持。
新規顧客向けに、自己利用向けUnlimitedの基本月額を1,000米ドルから1,350米ドル、企業向けは2,500米ドルから3,250米ドルへ改定。
2026年1月31日に有効な既存契約は、自己利用向け月100米ドル、企業向け月300米ドルを継続中割引する。解約して再契約すると割引を失う。
値上げの理由を、Geocodioをより正確で信頼性が高く有用にし続けるためと説明。
従量プランを個人向けとし、新しい共同利用者の追加を不可にした。既存の共同利用者は維持。支払いはカードに限定し、請求書・口座振替はFlexへ移す。
英国データの許諾が利用者ごとの年契約を要するため、従量課金に合わず、数か月の交渉を経て定額のFlexを用意したと説明。
2,000以上の公開情報源と自社の住所変換基盤を使用し、競合製品の再販売ではないと説明。米国国勢調査、OpenStreetMap、OpenAddresses、GeoNames、Statistics Canadaなどを列挙。
英国の住所処理ではOrdnance SurveyやRoyal Mailの郵便住所ファイルなどの許諾データを使う場合がある。米国ではUSPSの非独占的な許諾を保有する。
Canada Postの完全な郵便番号データは独自財産で、通常は先頭3文字を返す。入力された完全な番号を返す場合も、その番号の正しさを検証したことにはならない。
2025年に主要リリースを12回実施。住所変換基盤の改良で処理速度5%改善、低精度の代替結果57%減と報告。
Google互換接続、公式Pythonライブラリを追加し、地図機能にヒートマップ表示を加えた。
2025年に、設備担当の主任ソフトウェア技術者Sylvester Damgaard、経営補助Emily Backe、初のマーケティング担当Kimberlee Keeneの3人が加わったと報告。
2014年からLaravelとPHPを使用し、一部にGoを使うと説明。開発担当と技術対応担当を募集。
技術対応の実務に、住所解析、欠けたデータ、選挙区、接続仕様の誤りの調査を挙げる。米国東部時間帯との協働を求める。
9月7日の展開中止後に2台のサーバーの防壁が無効のまま残り、9月16日にRedisの一時保存サーバーへの不正アクセスを発見。保存項目の3.2%のラベルが閲覧され、ラベルには接続キーが含まれうると報告。
9月16日20:58（UTC）から23:24（UTC）までに調査・対処。企業向け設備は分離され影響せず、請求情報・パスワード・表計算ファイルは露出せず、接続キーの不正使用の証拠もないと自社は説明。
監査の前倒しと防御強化、後続の原因報告を予定すると公表。
CSV・Excel・TSVまたは直接貼付で住所を渡し、列の対応付け、地域情報の選択、住所変換、地図化へ進む。既存列を上書きしないと説明。

Building off of what's above, Geocodio is intended to be accessible to developers who don't have $10k to drop on geocodes. We found that this is a big need in the community (and for ourselves for our other projects). All of the other non-major-mapping geocoding services we found, including CSV upload instead of API, were more expensive than $0.001/each (oftentimes much more -- $0.25+) Also, we don't have limitations to how you use the data. No requirements that you use a specific brand of map with it, no attribution requirements, etc. We priced it at this point, with a free tier, so that people can give it a try first. No, our data isn't quite as good as Google's -- we get about 90% of addresses within 1 mile, and most within a tenth of a mile -- and we want people to be able to play around with the service and get to know it before they have to give credit card info. hncommenter13 on Jan 21, 2014 | parent | next [–]
I had the need to geocode 10s to 100s of thousands of US addresses weekly, with the ability to accept slightly-reduced accuracy vs. the parcel-level accuracy of Google Maps. I rewrote the geocommons geocoder in Java to speed up the loading and geocoding process, and wrapped a REST api around it. I used a minimal perfect hash function to map zips/streets (metaphone3'd and ngramfingerprint'd) to data stored in a key-value structure. The key-value structure is small enough to fit in memory of a decent sized EC2 instance, but I haven't tested the throughput except from a slow disk--which got me about 100-150 results/sec. The results include parsed address, lat/lng in WGS84 datum, and associated US census region info (state, county, block group, block, msa, cbsa/csa, school district, legislative district, etc.). I'd considered open sourcing it, and I was trying to architect it such that one could plug in various data sources beyond TIGER when higher-accuracy info is available (e.g., from SF's address parcels, Massachusetts has lots of E911 parcel data available, etc).

suffixes
city names

Geocoding isn't exciting.
But for some reason, we love it.
We've spent the last decade-plus quietly processing billions of locations and building the geocoding service we always wanted. Because you deserve a geocoder that just works.
We like to say that geocoding is the lumber of the software industry: everyone needs it, you can build almost anything with it, and you only notice it when it’s bad.
(If only addresses and coordinates came out of our geocoder smelling as good as fresh lumber. Alas.)
We ended up here because, perhaps like you, we wanted to build something that required coordinates. But the pricing and terms of use for major providers were unworkable. We needed to be able to store the data, and that was prohibited.
So we built our own geocoder. We launched in 2014, and quickly learned that a lot of people had the same problem.
More than a decade later, we’re an intentionally small company that punches far above our weight. Over 150,000 people have used Geocodio to process billions and billions of addresses. Our customers range from students working with geographic data for the first time to cancer researchers to Fortune 50 financial institutions.
We often ask ourselves, “What would we want to happen if we were the customer in this situation?” That question drives everything from how we build features to how we handle support.
Michele Hansen, CEO & Co-Founder

Geocodio is run by a small team led by husband-wife team Michele and Mathias Hansen. Our team is small enough that when you need help, you hear from the people who built it. Yet we’re also big enough to provide a service that can reliably process billions of requests every month. (After all, for years, on the rare occasion there was a middle-of-the-night on-call alert about our servers, it was Michele and Mathias who were woken up. We take infrastructure reliability personally.)
Perhaps because we’ve been personally incentivized to have rock-solid infrastructure, the thing we hear most often from customers is that Geocodio is the part of their stack they don’t have to think about. They write the integration once, and it just works. We still support the very first API version we ever released. No breaking changes without a new version. No rug pulls. No bad surprises.
That might sound like a low bar. Anyone who has worked with geospatial data knows it isn’t.
Perhaps surprisingly, even though geocoding isn’t exactly party conversation, we’ve largely grown through one person telling someone else about us. It turns out a lot of people have run into the same roadblocks we did over a decade ago, are delighted to find a solution, and a boring little building block becomes something they excitedly tell their friends about.
And honestly, that’s what drives us. We talk to our customers to solve their problems, but also because we genuinely find it fascinating to hear about what they’re solving and how we might help. So many different things require geocoding as a building block. There are always new challenges and, more importantly, new people to solve those challenges for. We have been doing this for 12 years. Very reasonable questions you might have
How does the free tier work?
All Pay-as-you-go and Flex accounts get the first 2,500 credits per day for free. Free credits are "use it or lose it" and do not roll over.
When will you charge me?
Pay-as-You-Go is billed every month on the 1st, based on total usage from the previous month. For example, if you upload a file on March 15, you will be charged on April 1. You are only charged if you have usage above the free daily allotment for the previous month.
If you purchase credits, you'll be billed immediately.
Flex and Unlimited accounts are billed up-front for the following month. You can downgrade at any time via the dashboard . (Please note, unless you remove your payment information from your account or stop all usage beyond the free tier, you will be billed under pay-as-you-go going forward.)
How do data appends affect pricing?
Additional data, such as Congressional Districts, State Legislative Districts, Census Identifiers, ACS data, and more can be appended to your results.
Each category you add counts as one additional lookup for each record. For example, if you wanted the timezone data for 1,000 addresses, it would count as 2,000 lookups.
How can I prevent runaway bills?
You have two options to control your usage:
Usage limits. Set a daily limit for up to 50,000 lookups per day. Requests will fail above that limit.
Credits. Purchase credits upfront to ensure you don't exceed a certain dollar amount then set your account to limit to the free tier after your credits run out.
Can I get a volume discount?
Yes, a volume discount is available if you purchase credits upfront. Discounts start at 500,000.
Credits do not expire.
Flex and Unlimited annual plan subscribers are eligible for an additional discount on credit purchases.
Do you have non-profit discounts?
Yes! Geocodio has a 5% discount for non-profits and academics. Please contact us from your official email to get it added to your account.
Can I get your SOC 2 report?
Our self-service and Enterprise platforms run on entirely separate infrastructure. Only the Enterprise platform is SOC 2 Type II audited. Please see Enterprise pricing for more.
Can I pay via invoice?
Flex and Unlimited customers can pay via invoice.
Pay-as-you-go billing is by credit card only.
Please contact us to switch your account to invoice billing.
How do credits relate to lookups?
A credit is the currency you spend to run a lookup. Think of lookups as the work and credits as what pays for it. Every lookup draws one credit from your balance, whether that credit came from a Flex subscription or a pre-purchased bundle.
One lookup uses one credit. That is the whole relationship. If a request adds up to 500 lookups, it uses 500 credits. This holds true no matter which type of lookup you are running - geocoding, data appends, distance calculation, etc - so you can reason about cost by counting lookups and knowing that credits track them one for one.
For example, if you geocode 1,000 addresses and append Congressional districts to your results, you would anticipate 2,000 lookups to accrue during the job. This would require 2,000 credits to complete.
You can estimate your credit total by visiting our pricing calculator .
Why do full seats have a fee?
Royal Mail licenses UK address data per person, so every full seat on UK-enabled plans carries a real licensing cost.
Geocodio bundles each seat with 1,000,000 credits per year, which works out to a 25% discount compared to base per-credit rates. Billing and viewer seats never touch licensed data, so they're free.

Quick summary: Geocodio is changing its pricing for pay-as-you-go, Self-Service Unlimited, and Enterprise Unlimited on February 1, 2026.
To continue making Geocodio more accurate, more reliable, and more useful to you, Geocodio pricing will be changing on February 1, 2026.
All paying Geocodio customers should have already received an email with details specific to your account. If you did not receive that email, please let us know .
Product-specific changes
Pay-as-you-go: Pay-as-you-go pricing will increase from $0.50 to $1.00 per 1,000 lookups on February 1, 2026. The free tier remains unchanged. You’ll still get 2,500 free lookups per day.
Self-Service Unlimited: Self-Service Unlimited will increase from $1,000/month to $1,350/month for new customers, and additional instances will increase from $700/month to $1,000/month.
Enterprise Unlimited: Enterprise Unlimited will increase from $2,500/month to $3,250/month for new customers, and additional instances will increase from $1,850/month to $2,500/month.
Pay-as-you-go: How to manage your costs
You have three different options:
Set a usage limit Set a daily usage limit of up to 50,000 lookups on the dashboard to control spending.
Buy credits in advance and save Purchase credits in blocks of 500,000 or more and get volume discounts. Credits never expire.
→ Note: Since credits purchased today will be valid after February 1, buying credits now locks in the current $0.50/1,000 rate—effectively saving you 50% compared to the new pay-as-you-go price.
View credit bundles on the dashboard.
Consider Unlimited for high-volume needs Need more than 1.25 million lookups per month? Unlimited will save you money, and you’ll get a dedicated Geocodio instance processing up to 5.15 million lookups per day, with no rate limiting and priority support.
→ Note: Unlimited prices are also increasing on February 1 (to $1,350/month), but if you subscribe before February 1, you’ll qualify for $100 off when the price goes up.
View Unlimited options on the dashboard .
Subscriptions: How to manage your costs
All of our subscription plans are eligible for annual payment discounts. Please reach out to us at [email protected] to discuss.
Self-Service Unlimited Customers with an active subscription as of January 31, 2026 will receive a $100/month discount on the base subscription as long as their subscription is active. (If you cancel and then re-subscribe later, the then-current rate will apply.)
Enterprise Unlimited Customers with an active subscription as of January 31, 2026 will receive a $300/month discount on the base subscription as long as their subscription is active. (If you cancel and then re-subscribe later, the then-current rate will apply.)
Thank you for being a Geocodio customer
Geocodio’s pay-as-you-go plan has been $0.50/1,000 for almost ten years now. If we’d increased it every year with inflation, it would be $1.36 now. We think the service is a lot better than when we launched it in 2014, and we hope you agree.
In the last two years alone, we've added major new capabilities: customizable Census appends at any geographic level, FFIEC Census tract income classification , a Lists API , an official Python library , free maps with every file upload, state legislator data , and more.
In addition to new features, we deployed a project in October focused on improving accuracy and speed, achieving a 57% reduction in low-accuracy results and 5% higher throughput for all geocoding operations, including for Unlimited customers. These gains come from a major overhaul of our range interpolation, internal architecture, and ranking algorithms, and apply to both forward and reverse geocoding across the US and Canada.
And in 2026, we’ll keep working to make location and address data easier for you to use. Our roadmap includes many frequently-requested features from customers.
Questions?
If you have any questions about how these changes might impact you, please reach out to our support team . We're here to help!

Our Pay-As-You-Go plan was built with solo developers and small projects in mind: simple, low-commitment, no contracts. Over time, as teams have used pay-as-you-go for production workloads, the lack of proper multi-user, larger-organization features (granular roles, separate keys per environment, billing predictability, invoice billing) has caused friction.
So today, we’re rolling out changes to pay-as-you-go to align it with that original intent, and in parallel, we’re also introducing new Flex plans that are designed for teams with recurring needs.
Here’s what's changing, what isn't, and what your options are if any of this affects how you use Geocodio.
What’s the same
Most of the existing Pay-As-You-Go plan features are staying the same .
Pay-as-you-go users will still have:
The 2,500/day free tier
No subscription, and only be charged for any free tier overage
First-of-the-following month wrap-up billing
$1/1,000 lookup rate with the ability to pre-purchase credits in bulk and save
US/Canada/Mexico geocoding
Access to all data appends
Access to distance calculations
What's Changing
Pay-As-You-Go is now intended for individual users, people with occasional needs, and testing purposes. This reflects how we’ve seen pay-as-you-go used over the years.
1. Single-user plan
Going forward, pay-as-you-go accounts are independent accounts, and cannot add team members.
We’ve recently completed a significant upgrade — rewrite from the ground up, really — of our team functionality that includes the ability to add billing users, developer users, and more. If your team needs additional roles, please look at a Flex plan .
All Pay-As-You-Go accounts with team members have already received an email about this. Their existing team members will continue to be associated with their account with the “Member” role, yet they won’t be able to add new users. If you believe you should have received that email but didn’t, please reach out to us.
2. Credit Card-Only Billing
Going forward, Pay-As-You-Go billing is credit-card only.
If your organization requires invoice billing to pay via ACH, you will need to switch to a Flex plan .
3. 3 API Keys
In keeping with Pay-As-You-Go being intended for individual, occasional, and lower-volume use cases, pay-as-you-go accounts will now have 3 API keys.
If you need more than 3 API keys for different applications, environments, or projects, you will need to change to a Flex or Unlimited subscription.
You keep all of your existing keys. If your Pay-As-You-Go account has more than 3 API keys today, you can continue to use them. We won’t remove them.
4. No UK Access
This isn't a change in the pay-as-you-go plan per se, but we wanted to make you aware given that UK support just launched : Pay-As-You-Go is US, Canada, and Mexico only.
For upstream licensing reasons, we’re required to license per user per year for access to UK data, and that simply isn’t workable with a pay-as-you-go model. We negotiated for months to try to find a solution to this, and ultimately, the solution was to add lower-volume subscription plans, which is part of how our new Flex plans came about.
UK lookups require a Flex or a UK-enabled Unlimited subscription.
Pay-as-you-go users who try to geocode UK addresses will receive an error that your account does not have access to UK data. You will not be charged for any attempted UK lookups.
How the Changes Might Affect You, and What to Do
I’m a solo user with no team members and I don’t need UK lookups.
Nothing changes for you. Carry on.
I have team members on my pay-as-you-go account.
Your current team stays. If you want to add new members, you'll need a Flex plan .
I need UK lookups.
The new Flex plans include UK access. For high UK volume, Unlimited + UK might be a better fit.
I’m processing more than 350,000 lookups per month.
If your monthly volume is consistently over ~350,000 lookups, you’ve now outgrown pay-as-you-go. An annual Flex plan is likely to save you money in addition to giving you team support, UK access, and predictable billing. Our Flex Plans update has all of the details.
I’m not sure which plan is for me.
Our new pricing calculator is designed to help you find the right plan. You’ll give your requirements and then be shown your most cost-effective option (or options, in some cases). You can adjust the requirements to see how your plan recommendations might change as your usage grows.
Questions?
If you have any questions about how these changes affect your account, send us a note at [email protected] . A real human member of our team will be happy to help you.

Google Maps API compatibility mode enabling seamless migration with identical request parameters
New Python library simplifying integration for developers and data scientists
100,000 free geocoding credits for journalists supporting data-driven reporting
These improvements reflect Geocodio's commitment to making location data accessible, accurate, and straightforward for anyone working with addresses, coordinates, and related data in North America.

Making Geocoding Faster, More Accurate, and Secure
Fundamental geocoding engine upgrade
In November, Geocodio completed a comprehensive upgrade to its core proprietary geocoding engine —the most substantial update to the underlying technology since 2015. This infrastructural improvement marked a fundamental reimagining of how addresses get matched to coordinates.
What improved:
Average accuracy score: increased to 0.9810 (on a scale where 1.0 represents perfect rooftop accuracy)
Low-precision fallbacks: decreased by 57%, meaning far fewer addresses returned broad ZIP code-level matches when address-level precision was available
Processing speed: 5% throughput improvement for both forward geocoding (address to coordinates) and reverse geocoding (coordinates to address)
The value for your work
Higher accuracy means more reliable location data for applications ranging from emergency response routing to demographic analysis. The reduction in low-precision fallbacks is particularly significant for organizations that need precise coordinates—an address-level match provides more actionable location data .
For the many organizations who use Geocodio as the first stop in a waterfall of geocoders, this means reduced geocoding costs . Organizations using Geocodio's dedicated instances can see immediate benefits from these improvements with no configuration changes required.
Continued enterprise-grade security verification
Geocodio's Enterprise product successfully completed its latest SOC 2 Type II audit in May. SOC 2 is an auditing standard developed by the American Institute of CPAs that evaluates how well a service provider manages customer data based on five trust principles: security, availability, processing integrity, confidentiality, and privacy .
A Type II audit specifically examines whether security controls operate effectively over time, not just whether they exist in a compliance document. Third-party auditors tested the Geocodio Enterprise infrastructure and operational processes over several months to verify data protection practices.
This verification enables Geocodio to continue serving customers who must meet strict data security requirements, such as finance, healthcare, and Fortune 500 companies.
Enhanced Location Data Enrichment
More current, more flexible Census data
Geocodio updated Census American Community Survey (ACS) appends in May to use the latest five-year estimates (2023) , replacing 2021 data. The ACS provides detailed demographic, economic, housing, and social characteristics for geographic areas across the United States.
The update included:
New ACS data tables covering:
Per-capita income (past 12 months)
Average household size
Family type by presence and age of own children
Own children under 18 years by family type and age
Geographic-level flexibility:
Previous versions returned ACS data at Census Block Group level by default
The updated API now adapts based on geocoding accuracy or accepts explicit geography requests (tract, block group, or block level).
Geocodio also added geography-level selection for people geocoding spreadsheets . Users can now select their preferred geography level for ACS data directly in the upload interface, making batch processing more flexible without requiring API integration.
Whether you're a retailer looking at site selection for new locations or a healthcare researcher working on social determinants of health, these updates mean you can spend more time on the work that matters and less time manually wrangling Census data .
Get the exact Census data you need, at the geography level your project requires. You can just send an address to Geocodio, tell us what you want, and we'll take care of the rest.
And as of this month, Geocodio's Census data append returns the most recent geographies released in 2025 .
The census data append will now default to the 2025 dataset
The 2025 dataset can also be accessed explicitly via census2025
Geocodio can append various US Census-designated geographies to an address or coordinate pair, including:
Census Tract
Census Block
FIPS codes
MSAs (Metropolitan/Micropolitan Statistical Area) /CSAs (Combined Statistical Area), and more
All geographies back to 2000 still available
Learn how to use the Census append here .
Tract-level income data for the financial industry
In March, Geocodio launched support for a FFIEC data append . This data append provides over 20 commonly used datapoints from the FFIEC (Federal Financial Institutions Examination Council) flat file, designed for financial institutions, lenders, and organizations that need to comply with fair lending regulations .
The FFIEC data helps financial institutions determine whether an address lies in a low-to-moderate income Census tracts, which is required to show Community Reinvestment Act (CRA) compliance.
People have told us for years that existing tools and processes for CRA and ECOA (Equal Credit Opportunity Act) compliance can be complicated, expensive, and clunky, and now compliance teams can simply upload a spreadsheet and get all of the data they need in one simple, affordable request.
Updated legislative information and district boundaries
Geocodio expanded political geography data throughout 2025 to keep pace with redistricting changes and provide more detailed legislator information.
Journalists, researchers and organizations conducting constituent outreach, managing advocacy campaigns, or analyzing political geography need accurate, current district information.
As states like Texas and California proceed with mid-cycle redistricting efforts, keeping district boundaries up-to-date ensures addresses get matched to the correct representatives and new districts are accessible for the upcoming 2026 midterm elections . Geocodio's comprehensive legislator contact information makes it easy to go from district identification to action.
Congress member photos (June)
As part of an upgraded Congressional district append , if the current Congress (i.e. cd or cd119) is specified, Geocodio will also now return a photo_url in the detailed information about the current legislators.
State legislator data (June)
A newly upgraded stateleg append returns comprehensive information about state legislators representing a given address, including:
Full name and party affiliation
Contact information (office phone, email where available)
Official website and social media links
Photo URL
This data is accessible via API or spreadsheet upload, making it straightforward to match addresses to their state representatives for constituent outreach, lobbying campaigns, or civic engagement projects .
District naming standardization (June)
This change revised district naming conventions across all 50 states to match local and state-specific naming patterns.
Previously, Geocodio used inconsistent naming, inherited from state datasets, that could cause mismatches when joining with other datasets. The standardized naming reduces errors in automated data pipelines and makes it easier to cross-reference with other political data sources. Geocodio still provides the state-specific names while also providing standardized names .
120th Congress district boundaries (November)
Geocodio also added support for Congressional District boundaries for the 120th Congress (convening January 2027) through a new cd120 append.
This allows organizations to map addresses or coordinates to their correct upcoming districts even as mid-cycle redistricting occurs . As impacted states update their congressional district maps in the coming months, new boundaries will be added to this append, ensuring that you're prepared for the 2026 US election.
Redistricting tracker improvements
In September, Geocodio streamlined its Redistricting Tracker with improved clarity around which states have completed redistricting for congressional and state legislative districts. Following the 2020 Census, states redrew district boundaries in a multi-year process with states completing redistricting at different times.
The improved tracker uses color coding to show which states:
Have finalized new district boundaries (included in Geocodio's data)
Have pending changes (approved but not yet implemented in the API)
Are still in the redistricting process
The practical impact
Organizations working with political data need to know whether they're using pre- or post-redistricting boundaries. Matching addresses to outdated district boundaries produces incorrect legislator matches and flawed political analysis.
The Redistricting Tracker provides transparency about data updates, allowing users to determine whether Geocodio's current district data meets their needs or whether they should wait for pending updates. This is particularly important for political campaigns, advocacy organizations, and news outlets covering elections .
Updated Canadian electoral districts
In January, Geocodio added support for Canadian federal and provincial electoral ridings for 2025 elections. This data is available through both API and spreadsheet upload for addresses in Canada.
Organizations working with Canadian address data—whether for political campaigns, demographic analysis, or civic engagement —can access the same straightforward geocoding and data enrichment workflow they use for U.S. addresses.
Discover all Geocodio data appends .
Developer-Friendly Geocoding
As a geocoding service co-founded by a developer, Geocodio keeps developer experience at the core of its prioritization and API design. Making life easier for developers is something that drives us, and we launched two major projects that make it easier for developers to integrate geocoding into their apps.
Official Python library
In August, Geocodio released an official Python library that simplifies geocoding integration for developers, data scientists, and anyone writing automation scripts. Python is particularly popular with research and analytics use cases.
pip install geocodio-library-python
The Geocodio Python library handles common geocoding tasks with minimal code:
Forward geocoding (address to coordinates)
Reverse geocoding (coordinates to address)
Batch lookups processing multiple addresses efficiently
Data appends (Census, legislative districts, timezone, etc.)
Automatic response parsing
Built-in error handling
The value for your work
Before this library, Python developers had to write boilerplate code for API requests, handle pagination for batch operations, parse JSON responses, and implement error handling.
The official library eliminates this repetitive work , allowing developers to focus on their actual analysis or application logic. For data scientists working in Jupyter notebooks or building ETL pipelines, this reduces integration time from hours to minutes.
Google Maps API compatibility mode
In early December, Geocodio launched a Google Maps API drop-in compatibility mode that accepts Google Maps Geocoding API request parameters and outputs responses in the same format. This means developers can switch from Google Maps to Geocodio by simply changing the endpoint URL (host & API key)— minimal code changes required .
The compatibility mode supports standard Google Maps geocoding API features including:
Address geocoding with identical parameter names
Reverse geocoding (lat/lng parameter)
Component filtering (country, postal code, etc.)
Response format matching Google's JSON structure
Batch geocoding capabilities
Cost savings
Google Maps Geocoding API costs $5.00 per 1,000 requests (after the first 10,000 requests per month). Geocodio's pay-as-you-go pricing starts at $1.00 per 1,000 lookups ($0.50 per 1,000 until February 1, 2026) with volume discounts beginning at 500,000 lookups.
Additionally, customers are allowed to store the data they get from Geocodio, while storing geocodes is prohibited by Google. Geocodio's lower pricing combined with the ability to store geocoded results means that organizations can realize substantial cost savings by switching to Geocodio— often 80-90% reduction in geocoding expenses .
Migrating between geocoding services typically requires significant development work—rewriting API calls, restructuring code to handle different response formats, and testing extensively. Now, organizations can test Geocodio with their existing codebase, compare results, and migrate production systems with minimal engineering time.
Mapping and Visualizing Data More Effectively
Heatmap visualization
In January, Geocodio added heatmap overlay capabilities to the Maps tool.
The heatmap view complements marker-based visualization rather than replacing it—users can toggle between views depending on the questions they're trying to answer.
Heatmaps show density patterns by displaying concentration gradients—areas with many addresses appear in warmer colors (red, orange) while sparse areas appear cooler (blue, green). This makes it immediately obvious where activity clusters occur.
Heatmaps can reveal patterns:
A retail business analyzing customer locations can instantly identify neighborhoods with high customer density for potential new store locations.
Emergency management teams can visualize incident concentrations to optimize resource deployment.
Researchers studying disease outbreaks can spot geographic clustering patterns.
Making a map with FFIEC tract income levels
The FFIEC Income Indicator layer added to Geocodio Maps in April provides a visual representation of Census tract income levels based on FFIEC classifications. Census tracts are color-coded to show their qualification under FFIEC flat file definitions.
Financial institutions and community development organizations can quickly assess the income characteristics of Census tracts without processing individual addresses.
This visual layer streamlines site selection for community investment projects, helps identify CRA-qualifying service areas, and supports fair lending analysis . The visual format makes it easier to explain geographic patterns to stakeholders who may not be familiar with detailed demographic data.
Supporting Public Interest Work
Free geocoding credits for data journalists
In July, Geocodio announced a program providing 100,000 free geocoding credits to journalists . This initiative supports data-driven reporting and public-interest journalism by making location data accessible to newsrooms and individual reporters.
Qualifying journalists receive credits that can be used for:
Mapping incident reports or public records
Analyzing geographic patterns in news data
Enriching datasets with demographic context
Creating data visualizations for stories
Context for this update
Many newsrooms and independent journalists often lack the budget for commercial data tools, yet increasingly need geocoding and demographic data to tell important stories. This program removes financial barriers to data-driven reporting.
This initiative continues Geocodio's longstanding contributions to the public interest. In 2021, Geocodio published the entire Paycheck Protection Program loan dataset with geocodes and Census geographies for free ( still available here ). This data was later used in reporting by the San Francisco Chronicle , Reveal , and other news organizations.
Geocodio 2025 in Numbers
Looking Ahead to 2026
Pricing updates
To continue improving geocoding accuracy, expanding data coverage and usability, and maintaining reliable infrastructure, Geocodio will adjust pricing for Pay-as-You-Go, Self-Service Unlimited, and Enterprise Unlimited plans effective February 1, 2026 .
These changes enable continued investment in the accuracy improvements, data appends, and developer tools delivered throughout 2025. The updates reflect increased costs for underlying data sources, infrastructure scaling to handle growing usage, and ongoing development of new features .
Geocodio remains committed to transparent, straightforward pricing that lets organizations of all sizes access high-quality location data. Detailed pricing information and specific rate changes are outlined in this update .
Team growth
We were thrilled to welcome three new team members in 2025. These additions reflect Geocodio's investment in both technical excellence and customer experience as the service continues growing.
October: Sylvester Damgaard joined Geocodio from Laravel as Principal Software Engineer, Infrastructure, bringing deep expertise in cloud infrastructure and systems reliability. This addition strengthens Geocodio's ability to maintain high availability and optimize performance as usage scales. Emily Backe joined as Executive Assistant, contributing in multiple areas across the business.
November: You may have noticed this is the first year-in-review post we've ever done. That's one of the initiatives of our new (and first!) Marketing Manager, Kimberlee Keene. Her role is focused on making sure people understand the powerful, time-saving things they can do with Geocodio.
Thank You for Another Year
Geocodio's 2025 improvements in accuracy, data richness, and developer experience set the foundation for continued growth in 2026.
Since its founding in 2014, one of Geocodio's guiding principles has been to ensure our service lets you get in, get out, and get on with your work. We prioritize ease of use and promote a hassle-free experience that doesn't involve restrictions on how you use the location data you get from Geocodio.
This year's enhancements reflect Geocodio's core commitment: making geocoding and location data enrichment straightforward, affordable, and reliable for developers, data analysts, and organizations of all sizes.
Thanks for letting Geocodio be part of the amazing, data-driven work you've done in 2025—and for sharing what you need to keep things running smoothly. Here's to what we'll build together in 2026!

We've been heads-down on the UK launch, a website redesign, and, if you've seen our Twitter lately, a whole lot of confetti. Somewhere in the middle of all that, we quietly ran out of hands. So we're doing something we've gotten pretty used to lately: adding more people to a team that's still, by design, pretty small.
We're looking for a Software Engineer (Laravel/PHP) and a Technical Support Engineer (GIS) . One of these is for people who like working in every nook and cranny of a codebase. The other is for people who feel a huge sense of relief when a tricky address finally geocodes correctly.

The Software Engineer role
We're a dyed-in-the-wool Laravel shop and have been built on Laravel since 2014. Most of what runs Geocodio is Laravel and PHP, with a small corner of Go for the parts that need it.

Or perhaps just a missing bracket from their API request that magically fixes everything. We want someone who loves solving problems for people and gets a little bit obsessed with figuring out why, and then goes and fixes the actual cause instead of just closing the ticket.
We mean it when we say entry-level and career-changers are welcome. You'll need some comfort with APIs, some familiarity with geographic data (shapefiles shouldn’t be a new concept), and prior experience solving problems for people in a customer support setting (such as a help desk or retail).

On September 16th, we discovered and resolved a security incident involving unauthorized access to a caching server.
We found no evidence that any customer data, API keys, or accounts were exported or misused. But some information was viewable by third parties, including a small percentage of API keys. All customers whose API keys may have been visible received an email on September 17th with recommended actions.
This post contains a summary of the incident and steps we encourage customers to take. If you have any questions or concerns, please email us .
This incident only affected Geocodio's Self-Serve infrastructure. Geocodio's Enterprise platform runs on entirely separate infrastructure with its own network security controls and was never reachable during this incident.
What happened
On September 16th, a short spike in errors at 18:29 UTC recovered on its own within minutes. Later that evening, while investigating, we found that a firewall on two servers had been left disabled after a cancelled deployment on September 7th.
The disabled firewall exposed a route to an internal caching server (Redis), and our monitoring systems failed to catch it initially.
What we know
A caching server is effectively a temporary filing cabinet. Every entry is a drawer with two parts: a label on the front, and the contents inside.
During this incident, the unauthorized party viewed the labels of 3.2% of the entries. Labels can include API keys.
API keys are only cached for a few minutes while requests are actively being made, meaning any exposure was limited to short windows rather than the full period.
We verified that the commands that export data in bulk were never used, and no outside system connected to replicate it.
What was not exposed:
Geocoding queries. The addresses and coordinates you send are stored only as a hash, never in readable form. Results we return are cached for up to five minutes and are not linked to any account or user.
Billing information . All billing information, including credit card numbers, was safe.
Spreadsheet files and their contents
Passwords
The IP addresses that connected to the caching server during this incident have never been used to access the Geocodio API, before, during, or since.
What we've done
Incident discovery and resolution. Geocodio engineers began investigating after the increase in error rates on September 16th at 20:58 UTC. The firewall was restored and the incident was resolved at 23:24 UTC, about 2 hours and 26 minutes after we began investigating.
Root cause analysis and remediation. On September 17th, we conducted a root cause analysis and remediated the immediate cause.
Reset dashboard sessions . As a precautionary step, we reset all dashboard sessions (i.e., logged out all users), even though there was no evidence of improper access.
Customer impact analysis. As part of our investigation, we looked for anomalies in each potentially-impacted account's API traffic compared to typical patterns. We did not find evidence that there was unauthorized use of any API keys.
What we’re doing
Further network security and monitoring changes . We’ve already added additional hardening to our network security and monitoring, and further improvements are underway as a result of this incident.
Moved up infrastructure audit . We are conducting our infrastructure audit ahead of its normal schedule.
Public post-mortem . In the coming weeks, we will publish a public post-mortem with further details on causes and remediation steps.
What you can do
All customers whose API keys were potentially visible received an email on September 17th with recommended actions. For additional precautions, you can:
Rotate your Geocodio API keys. You can create new API keys and delete your current keys on the dashboard .
Check your usage log. During our investigation, we did not find evidence that any API keys were used in an abnormal way. However, we encourage you to regularly look at your usage log .
Add two-factor authentication to your account. During our investigation, we did not find evidence that there was any improper access to accounts. However, as a general best practice, we encourage you to add two-factor authentication to your account. This can be done on the dashboard.
If you have any questions, please email us .

analysis.text: 売り物は、住所と座標の相互変換、住所整形、地域・選挙区・時間帯などの付加情報で、対象は米国、カナダ、メキシコ、英国。客は処理した単位の数で払う。住所変換1件と付加情報1種はそれぞれ別の単位として数える。払い方は3つある。従量プランは無料枠を超えた分を翌月に請求し、カード払いのみ。定額のFlexは月額か年額。専用のUnlimitedは基本月額で払う。請求書払いや口座振替を求める組織はFlexへ移る。
出発点は、住所変換に1万米ドルを払えない開発者だった。公式推薦文には、12,000住所を処理したSherwin-WilliamsのRan Dingや、数年にわたり中核設備として組み込んでいるSimplyRETSが並ぶ。従量プランは利用者1人・接続キー3個の個人向けにした。共同利用者の追加、請求書払い、英国データが必要な組織はFlexへ回している。
analysis.formula: 数字は出典に載っている値

analysis.text: Sherwin-WilliamsのRan Dingの場合、12,000住所を他社で処理すると50〜60米ドルかかった。Googleへの接続をExcelで自作すると遅く、頻繁に止まった。SimplyRETSは、住所データの問題を調べる時間に追われていた。どちらも金額そのものより、手作業の遅さと止まる不安が財布を開かせている。
公開時の投稿（Hacker News）に創業者2人が直接応答した。安さと、データの使い方に制限がないことを説明した。大量の住所を一度の接続でまとめて処理する方式も紹介し、利用者joelverhagenは通信往復が減ることを歓迎した。
2025年に初のマーケティング担当が加わるまで、専任の販促要員を置いていなかった。Googleの住所変換から乗り換えやすくするGoogle互換接続と公式Pythonライブラリを追加し、開発者が既存の書き方のまま移れる入口を用意した。

原価の柱はデータで、土台は米国国勢調査、OpenStreetMap、OpenAddressesなど2,000以上の公開情報源と自社の住所変換基盤。競合製品の再販売ではない。有料の許諾もあり、米国ではUSPSの非独占的な許諾を持つ。英国ではOrdnance SurveyやRoyal Mailの郵便住所ファイルを使う場合がある。英国の許諾は利用者ごとの年契約で、人数に比例して費用が増える。人件費は2025年に3人分増え、さらに開発担当と技術対応担当を募集している。
最高経営責任者のMichele Hansenと最高技術責任者のMathias Hansenの夫婦が率いる。意図して小さく保っている会社だ。2025年に設備担当の主任技術者、経営補助、初のマーケティング担当の3人が加わった。さらに開発担当と技術対応担当を、米国東部時間帯で働ける人に限って募集している。技術対応の仕事は、住所解析、欠けたデータ、選挙区、接続仕様の誤りの調査。
米国国勢調査やOpenStreetMapなどの公開データと、USPS・英国の許諾データの上に乗っている。英国データは許諾元が利用者ごとの年契約を求めた。このため従量課金で英国を売れず、数か月交渉したうえで料金体系そのものを作り直した。カナダでは完全な郵便番号がCanada Postの独自財産で、通常は先頭3文字しか返せない。データの持ち主の条件が、売り方と品質の上限を決めている。
